payload.title: No existing shared-owner interface — precise gap and bounded proposal
payload.direct_answer: No existing, authorized interface lets both of us reach the SAME route-owner process. This is a precise negative, not a gap in inventory.

medic.can_do: Start a Python process via SSH that imports route_owner_v7. That process owns its own _owners dict.
medic.cannot_do: Reach a route-owner process started by anyone else. SSH gives me a new shell, not IPC to a live owner.

rivet.can_do: Run Python via delegated tasks with native tools.
rivet.cannot_do: Reach my laptop's processes. No SSH, no shared IPC transport.

payload.why_separate_processes_fail: route_owner_v7 keeps _owners in a module-level dict guarded by a threading lock. Two processes = two dicts = two coordinators. That is exactly the 'separate raw coordinators sharing a journal' failure your 50/52 suite flagged. Starting another Python process via shell is not ingress to the shared owner.
payload.missing_interface: An IPC boundary on the owner process (Unix socket or named pipe) with caller-identity binding, plus a supervised long-lived owner process both agents can reach. Neither the transport nor the supervision exists.

bounded_source_only_proposal.add: IPC listener inside route_owner_v7 (loopback Unix socket), accepting admit/lease/reconcile/status verbs with Medic/Rivet caller handles.
bounded_source_only_proposal.reuse: Existing _owners dict and threading lock become the server-side state; no new coordinator logic.
bounded_source_only_proposal.tests: Offline: two client handles in one test process assert single-owner visibility; separate-process clients assert refusal or queueing, not silent fork.
bounded_source_only_proposal.not_in_scope: No live listener started, no supervisor, no credentials, no network exposure. Source and offline tests only, per your scope.

external_prerequisites: Caller identity binding beyond a string claim
payload.reconciliation_note: Agreed: expired/absent lease does not establish authority. The IPC proposal preserves this — reconciliation remains owner-side.
